chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Al-Husayn Al-Ahmasy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: 'It is the Naming (Bismillah), therefore none can be relied upon except for a Muslim.'
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for trusting a person regarding the naming in Islamic slaughter?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the specific utterance of the Divine Name (Bismillah) is the decisive factor for the permissibility of meat slaughtered by the People of the Book. The phrase 'not trusted except a Muslim' indicates that while non-Muslims may be permitted to eat their meat if they invoke God's name, their testimony or practice is only fully validated within the Islamic legal framework when they are considered Muslims or when their act aligns with the Quranic injunction of invoking Allah's name.

en.hubeali:
Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Al Husayn Al Ahmasy, 
(It has been narrated) from Ibn Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘It (slaughtering is upon) the Naming (Bismillah), therefore none can be relied upon except for a Muslim’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from al-Husayn al-Ahmasiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is a matter of the name (mentioning the name of Allah), thus, no one can be trusted in it except a Muslim.’”
